order_param_is_memory_copy.meaning: the order parameter passed to _updateLimitPostOrder is a memory variable (temporary copy), not storage

previous_tail_exists.meaning: a previous tail order exists in the limit price level to which the new order is being linked

new_order_prev_order_id_in_storage.meaning: stored prevOrderId of the new order after linking, i.e. the backward pointer recorded in storage

previous_tail_order_id.meaning: identifier of the previous tail order that the new order must point backward to

head_order_reassigned_incorrectly.meaning: the limit price struct's head order is reassigned incorrectly
head_order_reassigned_incorrectly.checkpoint: after order removal / linking in the limit price struct

assumptions: The order parameter being a memory variable means the backward pointer written to it does not persist to storage.
The previous tail order is the order the new order must point backward to in storage.
Head order reassignment correctness is observable in the limit price struct after linking/removal.

unresolved.description: Report does not state the concrete stored prevOrderId value or the previous tail order's identifier, so the equality is symbolic; no numeric binding is available.
Report does not specify whether the previous tail order is the head or a non-head order, nor the exact removal sequence that triggers incorrect head reassignment.

limitations: Only the incorrect_head_order_reassignment impact is formalized; other listed impacts are handled in separate passes.
The correspondence between stored prevOrderId and previous tail order id is symbolic; concrete identifiers are not supplied.
The head reassignment observable is a report-grounded Boolean because no numeric head-order value is given.
